issues.description: The problem specification and UML expect a method addGuestStudents(int) (single int parameter). However, the template Lecture.java provides a stub addGuestStudents(int, boolean) with an extra boolean parameter (validateInput). The solution implements addGuestStudents(int) (single parameter). This parameter mismatch in the template will confuse students and prevent them from implementing the method signature expected by the exercise and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's Lecture.addGuestStudents signature match the specification and solution by changing the stub to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to explicitly require the two-parameter signature if the boolean validateInput is intended.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution define an addGuestStudents method with a single int parameter (addGuestStudents(int)), but the template Lecture.java declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This signature mismatch (extra boolean parameter) creates a mapping barrier: students will implement or look for addGuestStudents(int) as specified by the exercise, but the provided template uses a different method signature, causing confusion and likely compile/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template method signature match the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* ... */ } (remove the boolean parameter).
